            PluginError::new(format!(
                "[cache] needs a Tokio runtime at startup to open its pool ({e})"
            ))
        })?;
        let url = self.url.clone();
        let cache = std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            scope
                .spawn(|| runtime.block_on(async move { PgCache::connect(&url).await }))
                .join()
                .map_err(|_| PluginError::new("the cache connection thread panicked"))?
                .map_err(|e| PluginError::new(format!("[cache] connecting: {e}")))
        })?;
        // The table is not created here. `brocanth-cache` can create it, and
        // it is off there for the reason it is absent here: the generator
        // proposes and the developer commits. `PgCache::schema_sql` hands out
        // the statements for a migration you can read.
        self.handle = Some(CacheHandle::new(Arc::new(cache)));
        Ok(())
    }

    fn provide(&self, cx: &mut ContextBuilder) {
        // `before_start` runs before the server is handed the application, so
        // the handle is here by the time any request builds a context.
        if let Some(handle) = &self.handle {
            cx.insert(handle.clone());
        }
    }
}
===== src/plugins/jobs/mod.rs =====
//! Background jobs, as this application registers them.
//!
//! A job is a struct that serialises, plus one `perform`. Enqueuing takes the
//! struct itself, so a payload a job cannot accept is a struct-literal error
//! rather than a decode failure on a worker at three in the morning.
//!
//! `brocanth-jobs` is in `Cargo.toml` because this file is here, and through
//! no other route. Delete the registration in `src/app.rs` and delete this
//! file, and the application runs no jobs and links nothing to run them with.
//!
//! # Enqueuing, and what does not work yet
//!
//! This plugin publishes the `Queue` on the per-request context, and a
//! handler in this project **cannot reach it today**. The `Ctx` in
//! `src/pages/mod.rs` carries the verb, the path, the parameters and the
//! partial depth, and has no extractor on it. `cx.extract()` works in
//! `plugins::announce!`, at startup, where the context builder is in
//! scope -- which is the one place this project calls it.
//!
//! So enqueue from `src/app.rs`, from a command under `src/commands/`, or
//! from anything else holding the `Queue`:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! queue.enqueue(Welcome { user_id: 7 }).await?;
//! ```
//!
//! The plugin half is right and the handler half is missing: `Ctx` needs
//! to carry the plugin context and expose an extractor. Until it does,
//! a line claiming otherwise would be a line that does not compile.
//!
//! # Where job types go
//!
//! `Welcome` is here so that this file compiles into something that runs.
//! Move it, and whatever follows it, into `src/jobs/` once there is more
//! than one -- the only thing that must stay here is the `register` call.
//!
//! **Register every job type before anything enqueues it.** A worker claims
//! by queue and not by name, so it will take a job whose name it does not
//! know, and a name it cannot resolve is a terminal failure: the row goes
//! straight to the dead letter rather than waiting for a worker that knows
//! it. The payload is kept and `Queue::requeue_dead` replays it, so nothing
//! is lost -- but the job does not run when you expected it to. During a
//! rolling deploy that means the old workers, so ship the registration
//! before you ship the first enqueue.
//!
//! The crate also ships `JobsPlugin`, and this is not that. `JobsPlugin` is
//! handed a queue that is already open, which is what an application with a
//! shared pool or a worker-only process wants. This one takes a URL, because
//! a new project has a URL.

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::{ContextBuilder, ProvidesContext};
use brocanth_jobs::{Job, JobContext, JobRegistry, Queue, Worker, WorkerHandle};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A job
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Says hello, slowly, somewhere that is not a request.
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Welcome {
    /// Who to welcome.
    pub user_id: i64,
}

impl Job for Welcome {
    const NAME: &'static str = "welcome";
    /// Which queue it waits on. The worker below claims from the queues the
    /// config names, so a job on a queue nobody claims waits for ever.
    const QUEUE: &'static str = "default";
    type Error = std::io::Error;

    async fn perform(&self, _cx: &JobContext) -> Result<(), Self::Error> {
        println!("welcome, user {}", self.user_id);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// Every job type this application can run.
///
/// The one list that has to be kept: a worker claims a row by name and needs
/// the type to decode it. Adding a job is a type above and a line here.
fn registry() -> JobRegistry {
    let mut registry = JobRegistry::new();
    registry.register::<Welcome>();
    registry
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The plugin
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[jobs]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// The database the queue lives in. Its own URL, not the models': a
    /// queue and an ORM can share one database and need not.
    pub url: String,
    /// Create the three tables at startup if they are absent.
    pub migrate: bool,
    /// Run a worker in this process, as well as enqueuing from it.
    pub worker: bool,
    /// Which queues that worker claims from.
    pub queues: Vec<String>,
    /// How many jobs it runs at once.
    pub concurrency: usize,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            url: "postgres://localhost/development".to_string(),
            migrate: true,
            worker: true,
            queues: vec!["default".to_string()],
            concurrency: 5,
        }
    }
}

pub struct Jobs {
    settings: Settings,
    /// Opened at `before_start` and not before, so this is an `Option` for
    /// exactly the length of the build.
    queue: Option<Queue>,
    /// Kept so the worker can be stopped. The core's shutdown hook lands
    /// with the server layer; until then, dropping the application stops
    /// the process and the worker with it.
    worker: Option<WorkerHandle>,
}

impl Plugin for Jobs {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = ProvidesContext<Queue>;
    const NAME: &'static str = "jobs";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self {
            settings: config,
            queue: None,
            worker: None,
        }
    }

    fn configure(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if self.settings.url.is_empty() {
            return Err(PluginError::new(
                "[jobs] url is required; the queue is a table and needs a database",
            ));
        }
        if self.settings.worker && self.settings.queues.is_empty() {
            return Err(PluginError::new(
                "[jobs] worker is true and queues is empty, so the worker would claim \
                 nothing; name a queue or set worker = false",
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn before_start(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        // The lifecycle hooks are synchronous and opening a pool is not. A
        // server process has a runtime, `block_in_place` is wrong on a
        // current-thread one, so take the handle and block the builder on a
        // scoped thread. This is startup, where blocking is expected.
        let runtime = tokio::runtime::Handle::try_current().map_err(|e| {
            PluginError::new(format!(
                "[jobs] needs a Tokio runtime at startup to open its pool ({e})"
            ))
        })?;

        let url = self.settings.url.clone();
        let migrate = self.settings.migrate;
        let queue = std::thread::scope(|scope| {
            scope
                .spawn(|| {
                    runtime.block_on(async move {
                        let queue = Queue::connect(&url).await?;
                        if migrate {
                            queue.migrate().await?;
                        }
                        Ok::<_, brocanth_jobs::Error>(queue)
                    })
                })
                .join()
                .map_err(|_| PluginError::new("the jobs connection thread panicked"))?
                .map_err(|e| PluginError::new(format!("[jobs] connecting: {e}")))
        })?;

        if self.settings.worker {
            // `enter` so that `start` finds the runtime to spawn on. The
            // worker is woken by the enqueue itself on Postgres rather than
            // polling; see `brocanth_jobs::listen`.
            let _guard = runtime.enter();
            self.worker = Some(
                Worker::builder(&queue)
                    .registry(registry())
                    .queues(self.settings.queues.clone())
                    .concurrency(self.settings.concurrency)
                    .start()
                    .map_err(|e| PluginError::new(format!("[jobs] starting the worker: {e}")))?,
            );
        }

        self.queue = Some(queue);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn provide(&self, cx: &mut ContextBuilder) {
        // `before_start` runs before the server is handed the application,
        // so the queue is here by the time any request builds a context.
        if let Some(queue) = &self.queue {
            cx.insert(queue.clone());
        }
    }
}
===== src/plugins/logging/mod.rs =====
//! Request logging.
//!
//! The core assumes no log layer at all -- not `log`, not `tracing`, not a
//! trait with a no-op default. This file is the whole of logging in this
//! binary: delete the registration in `main` and nothing logs, delete this file
//! and nothing about logging is compiled.

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, MiddlewareCatalog, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::NoContext;
use brocanth::routing::Next;

use crate::pages::{Ctx, Response};

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[logging]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// `error`, `warn`, `info` or `debug`.
    pub level: String,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            level: "info".to_string(),
        }
    }
}

pub struct Logging {
    level: String,
}

impl Plugin for Logging {
    type Config = Settings;
    /// Nothing on the context: a logger writes, it does not hand values out.
    type Provides = NoContext;
    const NAME: &'static str = "logging";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self {
            level: config.level,
        }
    }

    fn configure_router(&mut self, catalog: &mut MiddlewareCatalog<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        // Offered, not mounted. Where it runs is the application's call, made
        // in `main`, at a pattern this file never sees.
        catalog.offer("request_log", "one line per request: verb, path, status");
        Ok(())
    }

    fn before_start(&mut self, lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        eprintln!("[{}] level {}", lc.instance(), self.level);
        Ok(())
    }
}

/// The layer `request_log` mounts.
///
/// A plain function is a layer: `Layer` is implemented for anything callable
/// with a context and the rest of the chain. Not calling `next.run` is how a
/// layer short-circuits, and dropping it is all that takes.
pub fn layer(ctx: &mut Ctx, next: Next<'_, Ctx, Response>) -> Response {
    let verb = ctx.verb;
    let path = ctx.path.clone();
    let response = next.run(ctx);
    eprintln!("{verb} {path} -> {}", response.status);
    response
}
===== src/plugins/model/mod.rs =====
//! The model layer.
//!
//! The ORM is recommended and absent. SeaORM is the recommendation, it is not a
//! dependency of the core and never will be, and it arrives through
//! `brocanth-model` -- which is in `Cargo.toml` because this file is here and
//! through no other route. An application that stores nothing pays nothing for
//! it: not a crate in the lock file, not a section in the config, not a byte.
//!
//! The entity modules go under `src/models/`, from `brocanth generate model`.

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::{ContextBuilder, ContextItem, ProvidesContext};
use brocanth_model::ModelRegistry;

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[model]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// `sqlite://db/development.sqlite?mode=rwc`, or a Postgres URL.
    pub url: String,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            url: "sqlite://db/development.sqlite?mode=rwc".to_string(),
        }
    }
}

/// The handle a handler asks the context for.
pub struct Db {
    pub url: String,
}

impl ContextItem for Db {}

pub struct Model {
    url: String,
}

impl Plugin for Model {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = ProvidesContext<Db>;
    const NAME: &'static str = "model";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self { url: config.url }
    }

    fn configure(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if self.url.is_empty() {
            return Err(PluginError::new(
                "[model] url is required; there is no default database",
            ));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn before_start(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        // The pool opens here, at the last hook before the server is handed the
        // application, and drains on the matching shutdown hook.
        //
        // The registry below is what makes the generators and an admin UI
        // tractable: every entity compiled into this binary can be enumerated,
        // with its columns, nullability and keys. It is empty until the first
        // `brocanth generate model`, and the line is here so it is not a
        // surprise when it fills.
        let registry = ModelRegistry::new();
        eprintln!("[model] {} entities registered", registry.names().len());
        Ok(())
    }

    fn provide(&self, cx: &mut ContextBuilder) {
        cx.insert(Db {
            url: self.url.clone(),
        });
    }
}
===== src/plugins/openapi/mod.rs =====
//! The OpenAPI document, as this application derives it.
//!
//! The route table already knows every path, every verb and every path
//! parameter, and it knows them while this crate compiles, because the
//! filesystem is the route table. So the document is derived from
//! `crate::pages::router()` rather than written, and the two cannot drift:
//! add a file under `src/pages` and the document grows an operation.
//!
//! `brocanth-openapi` is in `Cargo.toml` because this file is here, and
//! through no other route. Delete the registration in `src/app.rs`, this file
//! and `src/pages/openapi.json.rs`, and the application describes nothing and
//! links nothing to describe it with.
//!
//! # What is derived, and what is not
//!
//! Every route, with its path parameters, an `operationId` and a 200. What a
//! page accepts and returns is not derivable from a `Fn(&mut Ctx)`, so bodies
//! are added by hand with `SpecBuilder::describe`, beside the
//! `routes_from_router` line below:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! .describe("/users/{id}", Verb::Get, |op| {
//!     op.summary("One user")
//!         .json_response(200, "The user", Schema::reference("User"))
//! })
//! ```
//!
//! `/openapi.json` is hidden from the document it serves. The endpoint is a
//! row of the table it describes, and an endpoint that describes itself is
//! noise in every client somebody generates from this.
//!
//! # Why this is not `OpenApiPlugin`
//!
//! The crate also ships `OpenApiPlugin`, and this is not that. That one is
//! handed a document that is already built, which is right for an application
//! that writes its document in `main`. This one takes a title and a version,
//! because a new project has a title and a version. It still holds an
//! `OpenApiPlugin` and calls its hooks, so the two things only that type can
//! do still happen: an invalid document stops the build, and the document
//! reaches `Services` for anything else that wants to read it.

use std::sync::OnceLock;

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::NoContext;
use brocanth::routing::Verb;
use brocanth_openapi::{Format, OpenApiConfig, OpenApiPlugin, SpecBuilder};

/// Where the document is served.
///
/// A constant and not a setting. The path is the name of the file in
/// `src/pages` that answers it, so moving the document is renaming that file
/// and this line, and a setting that disagreed with the file name would serve
/// a 404 and hide it in the document.
pub const ROUTE: &str = "/openapi.json";

/// The rendered document, both ways round.
///
/// Rendered once at `configure`, so a request costs a borrow rather than a
/// walk of the whole structure. A `OnceLock` because the page that serves it
/// is a plain function with no handle on this plugin.
static RENDERED: OnceLock<(String, String)> = OnceLock::new();

/// The document as JSON, or `None` when this plugin was never registered.
pub fn json() -> Option<&'static str> {
    RENDERED.get().map(|(json, _)| json.as_str())
}

/// The document as YAML, or `None` when this plugin was never registered.
///
/// Served by `src/pages/openapi.yaml.rs`, which is the file beside the
/// JSON one and reads this instead.
pub fn yaml() -> Option<&'static str> {
    RENDERED.get().map(|(_, yaml)| yaml.as_str())
}

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[openapi]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// The name of the API, which is not the name of this binary.
    pub title: String,
    /// The version of the contract, not of the crate.
    pub version: String,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            title: "My Blog".to_string(),
            version: "0.1.0".to_string(),
        }
    }
}

pub struct OpenApi {
    settings: Settings,
    /// Built at `configure` and not in `new`, because deriving a document can
    /// fail and `Plugin::new` cannot.
    served: Option<OpenApiPlugin>,
}

impl Plugin for OpenApi {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = NoContext;
    const NAME: &'static str = "openapi";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self {
            settings: config,
            served: None,
        }
    }

    fn configure(&mut self, lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        // The same function `src/app.rs` builds the live table with, so the
        // document describes what this binary actually dispatches.
        let router = crate::pages::router().map_err(|e| {
            PluginError::new(format!("[openapi] the route table does not build: {e}"))
        })?;
        let document = SpecBuilder::new(self.settings.title.clone(), self.settings.version.clone())
            .routes_from_router(&router)
            .hide(ROUTE, Verb::Get)
            .build()
            .map_err(|e| PluginError::new(format!("[openapi] deriving the document: {e}")))?;

        // The crate's own plugin, held rather than registered. Its
        // `configure` is what makes an invalid document a build failure
        // instead of a 500 found during an incident, and it renders both
        // bodies once.
        let mut served = OpenApiPlugin::new(OpenApiConfig::new(document).json_route(ROUTE));
        served.configure(lc)?;
        let _ = RENDERED.set((
            served.body(Format::Json).to_string(),
            served.body(Format::Yaml).to_string(),
        ));
        self.served = Some(served);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn register(&mut self, lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        // Publishes the document through `Services`, so a command or another
        // plugin can read it with `brocanth_openapi::document_of`.
        match &mut self.served {
            Some(served) => served.register(lc),
            None => Ok(()),
        }
    }
}
===== src/plugins/policy/mod.rs =====
//! Authorisation, as this application writes it.
//!
//! A rule is a predicate and a check is a witness. `PostPolicy` below is the
//! first; `Verified` is the second; the two are not alternatives.
//!
//! `brocanth-policy` is in `Cargo.toml` because this file is here, and through
//! no other route. Delete the registration in `src/app.rs` and delete this
//! file, and the application has no rule algebra and links nothing to have one
//! with.
//!
//! # The bug this file cannot have
//!
//! PocketBase validates a rule against an empty request object, so a
//! misspelled field in a negated rule becomes `'' IS NOT 'banned'`, which is
//! true, which grants access -- silently, for ever. Two things here make that
//! impossible, and both are visible below:
//!
//! 1. **A field name is not a string.** `Pred::eq` takes a `PostColumn`, so
//!    `PostColumn::Autor` is a compile error. There is no
//!    `Pred::eq("author_id", ..)` to fall back to and no string-to-filter
//!    parser anywhere in this framework.
//! 2. **An absent value is a word somebody wrote.** An `Option` does not turn
//!    into a `Bound`. The author writes `Bound::or_deny`, `or_allow` or
//!    `or_null`, and the word is in the diff for a reviewer to disagree with.
//!
//! # Where the rules go
//!
//! `Post` is here so that this file compiles into something that runs. Move
//! it, and whatever follows it, into `src/policies/` once there is more than
//! one -- what must stay here is the plugin, because that is what reads the
//! dialect and puts it on the context.
//!
//! The column enum is written by hand on purpose: the `policy!` macro is
//! deliberately late, after a real application has used the algebra, so that
//! the syntax is informed rather than imitated.
//!
//! # Listing, and then writing
//!
//! A list is a `WHERE` fragment, so the paginator keeps its totals:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! let rules: &Rules = cx.extract();
//! let condition = PostPolicy.list(&visitor).condition::<Post>(rules.dialect)?;
//! // "SELECT .. FROM posts WHERE " + condition.sql(), bound to condition.binds()
//! ```
//!
//! A write is the same predicate carried into the statement, which is what
//! closes the window between the check and the change:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! let admission = PostPolicy.update(&visitor).admission::<Post>(rules.dialect, id)?;
//! let rows = /* run admission.query(), count the rows */;
//! let verified = admission.resolve(rows)?;          // zero rows is a denial
//! let write = verified.update(rules.dialect, [(PostColumn::Status, "published".into())])?;
//! // run write.query(); then:
//! write.applied(affected)?;                          // zero affected is RaceLost
//! ```
//!
//! `Verified` is taken by value everywhere it is used, and a debug build fails
//! the test that checked one and then forgot to spend it.
//!
//! # This project also has the broker
//!
//! `Pred::audience` is the join, and it is why `brocanth-realtime`
//! depends on this crate. A predicate you can inspect inverts into an
//! audience -- `author_id = 7` becomes the key `(author_id, 7)` -- so the
//! broker files a subscriber under that key and one write is a map lookup
//! rather than one query per subscriber. A rule that is a string can only
//! be executed, which is why PocketBase runs the query.

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::{ContextBuilder, ContextItem, ProvidesContext};
use brocanth_policy::{Bound, Column, Dialect, Entity, EntityPred, FieldMask, Ident, Policy, Pred};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// An entity
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// The columns of `posts`, as an enum, because a rule is written in them.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub enum PostColumn {
    /// Primary key.
    Id,
    /// Who wrote it.
    AuthorId,
    /// `draft` or `published`.
    Status,
}

impl Column for PostColumn {
    /// Required rather than derived: a changed-field name that is not one of
    /// these is rejected instead of quietly permitted.
    const ALL: &'static [Self] = &[Self::Id, Self::AuthorId, Self::Status];

    fn name(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Id => "id",
            Self::AuthorId => "author_id",
            Self::Status => "status",
        }
    }
}

/// The table the rules below are about.
pub struct Post;

impl Entity for Post {
    type Column = PostColumn;
    /// Checked at compile time, because a table name is program text and the
    /// only honest moment to reject one is while the program is being built.
    const TABLE: Ident = Ident::must("posts");
    const PRIMARY_KEY: Self::Column = PostColumn::Id;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A subject, and the rules about it
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Whoever is asking. `brocanth-policy` never looks inside it.
///
/// An anonymous visitor is this application's own `None`, turned into a
/// decision at the point a rule reads it.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Visitor {
    /// The signed-in account, when there is one.
    pub account_id: Option<i64>,
    /// Whether this one may see everything.
    pub admin: bool,
}

impl Visitor {
    /// Nobody. What a request with no session carries.
    pub fn anonymous() -> Self {
        Self::default()
    }
}

/// The rules for `posts`.
///
/// Only `list` is required, because list authorisation is the one that cannot
/// be done per object: a paginator that filters after reading lies about its
/// totals. Everything else defaults to deny, which is what makes shipping this
/// file as it stands safe rather than lucky.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub struct PostPolicy;

impl Policy for PostPolicy {
    type Entity = Post;
    type Subject = Visitor;

    fn list(&self, who: &Visitor) -> EntityPred<Post> {
        if who.admin {
            // `Pred::is_always` reports this, so a test can assert which
            // subjects see everything.
            return Pred::Always;
        }
        Pred::any([
            Pred::eq(PostColumn::Status, "published"),
            // `or_deny` is the word that says what an anonymous visitor's
            // missing id means: they own nothing.
            Pred::eq(PostColumn::AuthorId, Bound::or_deny(who.account_id)),
        ])
    }

    fn create(&self, who: &Visitor) -> EntityPred<Post> {
        Pred::eq(PostColumn::AuthorId, Bound::or_deny(who.account_id))
    }

    fn update(&self, who: &Visitor) -> EntityPred<Post> {
        if who.admin {
            return Pred::Always;
        }
        Pred::eq(PostColumn::AuthorId, Bound::or_deny(who.account_id))
    }

    fn writable(&self, who: &Visitor) -> FieldMask<PostColumn> {
        if who.admin {
            FieldMask::except([PostColumn::Id])
        } else {
            // The author edits the body, never the status. The mask is the
            // other half of the rule: `update` says which rows, this says
            // which columns.
            FieldMask::only([PostColumn::AuthorId])
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The plugin
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[policy]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// `postgres` or `sqlite`. A string here and an enum below: a config file
    /// is text, and the translation is checked at startup where a typo can
    /// still be answered.
    pub dialect: String,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            dialect: "sqlite".to_string(),
        }
    }
}

/// What this plugin puts on the context.
///
/// The dialect, and only the dialect. Every compile entry point still takes
/// one as an argument -- the call site says which it meant -- and this is
/// where the call site gets it, so one database is named once.
///
/// The policies are not here. `PostPolicy` is a unit struct and a value, not
/// a service: a handler writes `PostPolicy.list(&who)` and has nothing to
/// look up. What a handler cannot work out on its own is which dialect this
/// deployment is, so that is what the context carries.
pub struct Rules {
    /// Which dialect this application's conditions are compiled for.
    pub dialect: Dialect,
}

impl ContextItem for Rules {}

pub struct Policies {
    settings: Settings,
    /// Read at `configure` and not in `new`, because turning a string into a
    /// dialect can fail and `Plugin::new` cannot.
    dialect: Option<Dialect>,
}

impl Plugin for Policies {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = ProvidesContext<Rules>;
    const NAME: &'static str = "policy";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self {
            settings: config,
            dialect: None,
        }
    }

    fn configure(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let dialect = match self.settings.dialect.as_str() {
            "postgres" => Dialect::Postgres,
            "sqlite" => Dialect::Sqlite,
            other => {
                return Err(PluginError::new(format!(
                    "[policy] dialect is {other:?}; write postgres or sqlite"
                )))
            }
        };

        // Compile one rule at startup. It costs a string and it answers the
        // only question this file can get wrong without anybody noticing: a
        // column whose name is not a bare identifier fails the query rather
        // than escaping into it, and finding that out here is better than
        // finding it out on the first list request.
        let condition = PostPolicy
            .list(&Visitor::anonymous())
            .condition::<Post>(dialect)
            .map_err(|e| PluginError::new(format!("[policy] posts: {e}")))?;
        eprintln!("[policy] posts, anonymous: {}", condition.sql());

        self.dialect = Some(dialect);
        Ok(())
    }

    fn provide(&self, cx: &mut ContextBuilder) {
        // `configure` runs before the server is handed the application, so
        // the dialect is here by the time any request builds a context.
        if let Some(dialect) = self.dialect {
            cx.insert(Rules { dialect });
        }
    }
}
===== src/plugins/realtime/mod.rs =====
//! The realtime broker, as this application registers it.
//!
//! A subscription is an index entry, not a query. `brocanth-policy` is a
//! value rather than a string, so "the owner" inverts into `(author_id, 7)`,
//! the broker files the subscriber under that key, and a write becomes a map
//! lookup. PocketBase runs one `SELECT` per subscriber instead, which is
//! about 180 ms on Postgres at six hundred of them.
//!
//! `brocanth-realtime` is in `Cargo.toml` because this file is here, and
//! through no other route. Delete the registration in `src/app.rs` and delete
//! this file, and the application broadcasts nothing and links nothing to do
//! it with.
//!
//! # Publishing
//!
//! A handler that just wrote a row has the row, so it hands it over and the
//! broker reads nothing:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! // Not from a handler yet: `Ctx` has no extractor. See below.
//! let realtime: &Broadcast = cx.extract();
//! let row = Row::new().with("author_id", author);
//! realtime
//!     .broker
//!     .publish_with_row(&RowChange::created("posts", id), &row);
//! ```
//!
//! `src/app.rs` extracts it once at startup and prints the client limit,
//! which is there to be deleted: it exists so a brand-new project reads the
//! value it was given rather than warning that nothing does.
//!
//! # Reading
//!
//! The broker stops one layer short of the socket, on purpose: this
//! application's `Response` is a complete `Vec<u8>`, and every response hook
//! is specified to see one. A streaming body would skip compression, the
//! partial-navigation headers and `ETag` without saying so, so server-sent
//! events are a change to the core's hook contract rather than a type change
//! here.
//!
//! Three things read a mailbox today, none of them needing that change:
//!
//! 1. **In process.** `Broker::connect`, one subscription, and a thread on
//!    `Mailbox::recv_blocking`. This is how a cache invalidator or an audit
//!    log is written, and it is the reason to have a broker before there is a
//!    transport at all.
//! 2. **Long polling.** Keep the `Client` in the session; each request calls
//!    `Mailbox::recv_timeout` for a few seconds, then `Mailbox::drain`, and
//!    returns the frames as one finished body. Every hook runs exactly as
//!    specified. It costs a request per interval and a little latency.
//! 3. **Nothing.** The index costs what it holds, and an application that
//!    publishes without subscribers pays for a map lookup that finds no one.

use std::sync::Arc;

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::{ContextBuilder, ContextItem, ProvidesContext};
use brocanth_realtime::{Broker, Config, Overflow};

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[realtime]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// How many connections the broker will hold. At the limit `connect`
    /// refuses rather than evicting, so a new socket cannot displace an
    /// established one.
    pub max_clients: usize,
    /// How many topics one client may hold, so a client cannot spend the
    /// server's memory by asking.
    pub max_subscriptions_per_client: usize,
    /// How many frames a mailbox holds before the overflow policy fires.
    pub queue: usize,
    /// `drop-oldest`, `drop-newest` or `disconnect`. A string here and an
    /// enum below: the config file is text, and the translation is checked
    /// at startup where a typo can still be answered.
    pub overflow: String,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            max_clients: 1000,
            max_subscriptions_per_client: 64,
            queue: 32,
            overflow: "drop-oldest".to_string(),
        }
    }
}

/// What this plugin puts on the context.
///
/// A wrapper and not `Arc<Broker>` itself, because `ContextItem` is
/// brocanth's trait and `Broker` is `brocanth-realtime`'s type. That crate
/// deliberately does not depend on the core -- nothing in it touches a
/// request, a response or a route -- so the impl that joins the two belongs
/// in the one crate that can see both, which is this one.
pub struct Broadcast {
    /// The broker. Shared, so a clone is a pointer and every request sees
    /// the same index.
    pub broker: Arc<Broker>,
}

impl ContextItem for Broadcast {}

pub struct Realtime {
    settings: Settings,
    /// Built at `configure` and not in `new`, because reading the overflow
    /// policy out of a string can fail and `Plugin::new` cannot.
    broker: Option<Arc<Broker>>,
}

impl Plugin for Realtime {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = ProvidesContext<Broadcast>;
    const NAME: &'static str = "realtime";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self {
            settings: config,
            broker: None,
        }
    }

    fn configure(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let overflow = match self.settings.overflow.as_str() {
            "drop-oldest" => Overflow::DropOldest,
            "drop-newest" => Overflow::DropNewest,
            "disconnect" => Overflow::Disconnect,
            other => {
                return Err(PluginError::new(format!(
                    "[realtime] overflow is {other:?}; write drop-oldest, \
                     drop-newest or disconnect"
                )))
            }
        };
        if self.settings.queue == 0 {
            return Err(PluginError::new(
                "[realtime] queue must hold at least one frame",
            ));
        }
        if self.settings.max_clients == 0 {
            return Err(PluginError::new(
                "[realtime] max_clients is 0, so every connection is refused",
            ));
        }
        // Synchronous, allocating a few maps, needing no runtime. Unlike a
        // pool, there is nothing here to open, so there is no `before_start`.
        self.broker = Some(
            Broker::builder()
                .config(Config {
                    max_clients: self.settings.max_clients,
                    max_subscriptions_per_client: self.settings.max_subscriptions_per_client,
                    queue: self.settings.queue,
                    overflow,
                })
                .build(),
        );
        Ok(())
    }

    fn provide(&self, cx: &mut ContextBuilder) {
        // `configure` runs before the server is handed the application, so
        // the broker is here by the time any request builds a context.
        if let Some(broker) = &self.broker {
            cx.insert(Broadcast {
                broker: broker.clone(),
            });
        }
    }
}
===== src/plugins/sessions/mod.rs =====
//! Cookie sessions, and the one value they put on the context.

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, MiddlewareCatalog, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::{ContextBuilder, ContextItem, ProvidesContext};
use brocanth::routing::Next;

use crate::pages::{Ctx, Response};

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[sessions]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    pub cookie: String,
    /// `Secure`, so the cookie never leaves over plain HTTP. False in
    /// development and nowhere else.
    pub secure: bool,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            cookie: "_my_blog_session".to_string(),
            secure: true,
        }
    }
}

/// What this plugin puts on the context.
///
/// One provider owns one type, so there is no string name to misspell and no
/// `responds_to?` guard to forget. A handler that asks for a `Session` in an
/// application that never registered this plugin does not compile.
#[derive(Debug, Default)]
pub struct Session {
    pub cookie: String,
}

impl ContextItem for Session {}

pub struct Sessions {
    cookie: String,
    secure: bool,
}

impl Plugin for Sessions {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = ProvidesContext<Session>;
    const NAME: &'static str = "sessions";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self {
            cookie: config.cookie,
            secure: config.secure,
        }
    }

    fn configure(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if self.cookie.is_empty() {
            // A missing or ill-typed key fails at startup, not at first use,
            // and the plugin never quietly chooses a name the operator did not.
            return Err(PluginError::new("[sessions] cookie must not be empty"));
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn configure_router(&mut self, catalog: &mut MiddlewareCatalog<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        catalog.offer(
            "session",
            "reads the cookie and puts a Session on the context",
        );
        Ok(())
    }

    fn before_start(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if !self.secure {
            eprintln!("[sessions] Secure is off: development only");
        }
        Ok(())
    }

    fn provide(&self, cx: &mut ContextBuilder) {
        cx.insert(Session {
            cookie: self.cookie.clone(),
        });
    }
}

/// The layer `session` mounts. Reading the cookie off the request and writing
/// `Set-Cookie` on the way out both need the request type that arrives with the
/// HTTP server; the seam is here and it is already the right shape.
pub fn layer(ctx: &mut Ctx, next: Next<'_, Ctx, Response>) -> Response {
    next.run(ctx)
}
===== src/plugins/storage/mod.rs =====
//! File storage, as this application registers it.
//!
//! An object is named by what is in it. Thirty-two bytes rendered as
//! sixty-four hex characters is the whole address, so `..`, a slash and a
//! drive letter are not values the type can hold and no filename a client
//! sent ever becomes a path component. The original name is kept as metadata,
//! defanged for the `Content-Disposition` header it ends up in, and never
//! touches the filesystem.
//!
//! `brocanth-storage` is in `Cargo.toml` because this file is here, and
//! through no other route. Delete the registration in `src/app.rs` and delete
//! this file, and the application stores no files and links nothing to store
//! them with.
//!
//! # Uploading
//!
//! There is no upload route here, on purpose: `brocanth-storage` parses no
//! multipart body and knows nothing about HTTP, and whether *this*
//! application lets *this* request store a file is a policy question a
//! generator cannot answer. A handler that has already asked it writes:
//!
//! ```ignore
//! let files: &FileStore = cx.extract();
//! let about = ObjectInfo::new()
//!     .with_filename(sent_name)
//!     .with_declared_type(sent_type);
//! let key = files.store.put(&bytes, &about).await?;
//! ```
//!
//! and keeps `key.to_hex()` on the record. The media type is taken from the
//! bytes rather than from `sent_type`, because a client that labels a file
//! `text/html` is choosing what this origin serves back to the next visitor.
//!
//! # Serving
//!
//! Also the application's, and for a sharper reason: a file token says "the
//! bearer may read this object" and carries no identity at all. Mint one only
//! for a request that has already passed the policy, because after that the
//! token is the only thing between the object and whoever the URL reaches.
//!
//! ```ignore
//! let token = files.tokens.issue(&key);           // after the policy said yes
//! let key = files.tokens.verify(presented)?;      // on the download route
//! let meta = files.store.meta(&key).await?;
//! ```
//!
//! `ObjectMeta::content_type` answers `is_safe_to_inline`, which is the bit
//! the download route needs to force an attachment for everything that is not
//! a recognised image.
//!
//! # Thumbnails
//!
//! `get_variant` and `put_variant` are here already, with the `variants`
//! feature off: moving derived bytes needs no codec, so this build can serve
//! a variant another process computed and cannot compute one itself. Turning
//! the feature on in `Cargo.toml` adds `derive_variant`, and adds png, jpeg,
//! gif and webp decoders pointed at stranger-supplied bytes. An application
//! that stores documents should leave it off.
//!
//! # One secret, two keys
//!
//! `secret` below is used twice and the two uses cannot be confused for each
//! other: `HashKey` and `FileTokenKey` derive from it under different domain
//! separators, so an address key cannot sign a token and a token key cannot
//! address an object. Rotating the secret invalidates every outstanding token
//! at once, which is the break-glass, and it also changes the address new
//! uploads are stored at -- objects already on disk keep the address they
//! were written under, so rotate it with a plan rather than on a Friday.

use std::sync::Arc;

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::{ContextBuilder, ContextItem, ProvidesContext};
use brocanth_storage::{FileTokenKey, FileTokens, HashKey, LocalDisk, Storage};

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[storage]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// Where the objects live, relative to the working directory or absolute.
    /// Created if it is not there.
    pub root: String,
    /// The deployment secret. It signs file tokens and keys object addresses;
    /// see the module header for what each of those means.
    pub secret: String,
    /// How many seconds a file token lives. A token cannot be revoked, so
    /// this is the leak window.
    pub token_ttl: i64,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            root: "var/uploads".to_string(),
            secret: "development only: replace before anything is uploaded in anger".to_string(),
            token_ttl: 120,
        }
    }
}

/// What this plugin puts on the context.
///
/// A wrapper and not the two values loose, because `ContextItem` is
/// brocanth's trait and both of these are `brocanth-storage`'s types. That
/// crate deliberately does not depend on the core -- it has no routes, parses
/// no multipart body and knows nothing about HTTP -- so the impl that joins
/// the two belongs in the one crate that can see both, which is this one.
pub struct FileStore {
    /// The store, behind the trait rather than as a `LocalDisk`, so swapping
    /// the backend is a change in this file and nowhere else.
    ///
    /// Allowed to be unread, and only until one thing changes. Every
    /// `Storage` method is `async` and the startup line below is not, so
    /// nothing the generator writes can touch this field — a handler is
    /// what uses it, and a handler cannot reach the per-request context
    /// yet, because `Ctx` in `src/pages/mod.rs` has no extractor. Delete
    /// this attribute the moment you write the first upload route; it is
    /// a note about today, not about the field.
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    pub store: Arc<dyn Storage>,
    /// Mints and verifies the short-lived tokens a download route checks.
    pub tokens: FileTokens,
}

impl ContextItem for FileStore {}

pub struct Files {
    settings: Settings,
    /// Built at `configure`, because opening a store can fail and
    /// `Plugin::new` cannot.
    store: Option<Arc<dyn Storage>>,
    tokens: Option<FileTokens>,
}

impl Plugin for Files {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = ProvidesContext<FileStore>;
    const NAME: &'static str = "storage";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self {
            settings: config,
            store: None,
            tokens: None,
        }
    }

    fn configure(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        if self.settings.root.is_empty() {
            return Err(PluginError::new(
                "[storage] root is required; there is no default directory",
            ));
        }
        if self.settings.secret.is_empty() {
            // An empty secret is not a weaker store, it is two different
            // stores: addresses stop being keyed, and a token key of no bytes
            // signs tokens anybody can forge.
            return Err(PluginError::new(
                "[storage] secret is required; it signs file tokens and keys object addresses",
            ));
        }
        if self.settings.token_ttl <= 0 {
            return Err(PluginError::new(
                "[storage] token_ttl must be at least one second, or no token is ever valid",
            ));
        }
        // Synchronous: `std::fs`, a `create_dir_all` and a `canonicalize`.
        // Unlike a pool there is nothing to open, so there is no
        // `before_start`.
        let disk = LocalDisk::open(&self.settings.root)
            .map_err(|e| {
                PluginError::new(format!("[storage] opening {:?}: {e}", self.settings.root))
            })?
            .with_hash_key(HashKey::from_secret(self.settings.secret.as_bytes()));
        self.store = Some(Arc::new(disk));
        self.tokens = Some(
            FileTokens::new(FileTokenKey::from_secret(self.settings.secret.as_bytes()))
                .with_ttl(self.settings.token_ttl),
        );
        Ok(())
    }

    fn provide(&self, cx: &mut ContextBuilder) {
        // `configure` runs before the server is handed the application, so
        // both are here by the time any request builds a context.
        if let (Some(store), Some(tokens)) = (&self.store, &self.tokens) {
            cx.insert(FileStore {
                store: store.clone(),
                tokens: tokens.clone(),
            });
        }
    }
}
===== src/plugins/validation/mod.rs =====
//! Request validation, as this application registers it.
//!
//! The shape of a schema is checked when this crate compiles; the data is
//! checked when a request arrives, because a request body is bytes that did
//! not exist at compile time. What the derive buys is that the check and the
//! description come from one declaration, so a form, an OpenAPI document and
//! the check on the way in cannot drift apart.
//!
//! `brocanth-schema` is in `Cargo.toml` because this file is here, and
//! through no other route. Delete the registration in `src/app.rs` and delete
//! this file, and the application validates nothing and links nothing to
//! validate with.
//!
//! # The proof, and why a handler asks for it
//!
//! `Valid<T>` has a private field and exactly one constructor:
//! `Validation::check`, a method on the context item this plugin provides.
//! A handler that takes a `Valid<SignUp>` therefore has proof the body was
//! checked, and a handler in an application that never registered this plugin
//! does not compile. Forgetting to wire validation is a build that does not
//! finish rather than a bug that reaches production.
//!
//! ```ignore
//! let checks: &brocanth_schema::Validation = cx.extract();
//! match checks.check(SignUp { username, email }) {
//!     Ok(body) => create(body),
//!     Err(issues) => Response {
//!         status: 422,
//!         body: checks.render(&issues),
//!         ..Default::default()
//!     },
//! }
//! ```
//!
//! # Where schemas go
//!
//! `SignUp` is here so that this file compiles into something that runs. Move
//! it, and whatever follows it, into `src/schemas/` once there is more than
//! one. Nothing registers a schema: a type with `#[derive(Validate)]` is
//! reachable from wherever it is written.
//!
//! # The middleware this does not mount
//!
//! `ValidationPlugin` offers a middleware called `validation.report`, and
//! this plugin does not pass the offer on. The offer is a name; the crate
//! ships no function behind it, because turning an unhandled report into a
//! 422 means knowing what this application's `Response` is. Mounting a name
//! with no layer behind it stops the application at startup, so the offer is
//! withheld until there is something to mount. Write the layer in this file,
//! add `"validation.report" => Some(validation::layer),` to
//! `src/plugins/mod.rs`, and forward `configure_router` to `self.inner`.

use brocanth::plugin_api::{Lifecycle, Plugin, PluginError};
use brocanth::plugin_context::{ContextBuilder, ProvidesContext};
use brocanth_schema::{ReportStyle, Validate, ValidationConfig, ValidationPlugin};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// A schema
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// What somebody may send to sign up.
///
/// A constraint that cannot mean anything for a field's type does not
/// compile, and neither does a rule naming a field this struct does not have:
/// the derive reads the field list from the struct, so there is no string to
/// misspell.
#[derive(Debug, Validate)]
/// The shape a sign-up body has to have.
///
/// Allowed to be unconstructed: a handler is what builds one, and a
/// handler cannot reach the per-request context yet — `Ctx` in
/// `src/pages/mod.rs` has no extractor, so `Valid<SignUp>` has nowhere to
/// be asked for. Delete this attribute with the first route that takes a
/// body.
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub struct SignUp {
    /// Three to thirty-two characters.
    #[validate(string(min_length = 3, max_length = 32))]
    pub username: String,
    /// Checked against the shape of an address, not against a mail server.
    #[validate(string(email))]
    pub email: String,
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The plugin
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// What this plugin is built from.
///
/// It derives `Deserialize` because this application reads it from
/// `[validation]` in a TOML file. Drop the config plugin and the derive goes
/// with it: `Plugin::Config` carries no bounds the core imposes.
#[derive(Debug, serde::Deserialize)]
#[serde(default, deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct Settings {
    /// `json` or `form`. A string here and an enum below: the config file is
    /// text, and the translation is checked at startup where a typo can still
    /// be answered.
    pub report: String,
}

impl Default for Settings {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            report: "json".to_string(),
        }
    }
}

pub struct Validation {
    report: String,
    /// Built at `configure` and not in `new`, because reading the report
    /// style out of a string can fail and `Plugin::new` cannot.
    inner: Option<ValidationPlugin>,
}

impl Plugin for Validation {
    type Config = Settings;
    type Provides = ProvidesContext<brocanth_schema::Validation>;
    const NAME: &'static str = "validation";

    fn new(config: Settings) -> Self {
        Self {
            report: config.report,
            inner: None,
        }
    }

    fn configure(&mut self, _lc: &mut Lifecycle<'_>) -> Result<(), PluginError> {
        let report = match self.report.as_str() {
            "json" => ReportStyle::Json,
            "form" => ReportStyle::Form,
            other => {
                return Err(PluginError::new(format!(
                    "[validation] report is {other:?}; write json or form"
                )))
            }
        };
        // The crate's own plugin, held rather than registered: it is the only
        // thing that can build the context item, because `Validation`'s field
        // is private and this file is not that crate.
        self.inner = Some(ValidationPlugin::new(ValidationConfig { report }));
        Ok(())
    }

    fn provide(&self, cx: &mut ContextBuilder) {
        // `configure` runs before the server is handed the application, so
        // the inner plugin is here by the time any request builds a context.
        if let Some(inner) = &self.inner {
            inner.provide(cx);
        }
    }
}
===== AGENTS.md =====
<!-- Written by `brocanth`. Do not edit -- `brocanth add` rewrites this file. -->
<!-- Notes of your own go in a file of your own, beside this one. -->
# Working in My Blog

A brief for a coding agent. Written by `brocanth`, so the lists
below are this project's and not the framework's in general.

## Check your work

Run these after every change, in this order. They are ordered by how
fast they fail.

```
cargo test
cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo fmt --check
```

The route table is `pages::router()` and the test beside it asserts the
shape of the directory. Read it rather than guessing what covers a
request.

## What this binary contains

- `core`  the router, the context, the plugin seams
- `logging`  a line per request; the core assumes no log layer
- `config`  config/<env>.toml, merged; without it nothing links a TOML parser
- `sessions`  a cookie, and a `Session` the context hands a handler
- `model`  SeaORM, validations, migrations; without it no SQL driver at all
- `cache`  a cache on an unlogged Postgres table, not Redis; without it no cache at all
- `jobs`  a queue in Postgres with retries and a dead letter; a worker in this process
- `auth`  argon2id accounts and signed sessions; no provider, so no HTTP client
- `policy`  typed predicates over an entity's columns; no ORM, no driver, no core
- `storage`  uploads on a local disk, addressed by content hash; no object store and no S3
- `input`  a form or a JSON body, read into a struct, with every fault at once
- `middleware`  proxy headers, method override, canonical host, content types, CORS
- `openapi`  an OpenAPI 3.1 document derived from src/pages, served at /openapi.json
- `validation`  a zod-shaped vocabulary; a handler takes Valid<T> or does not compile
- `realtime`  one write is a map lookup, not a query per subscriber; no transport yet
- `commands`  this project's own command line, `serve` plus whatever you add
- `rsx`  `.rsx` templates compiled into the binary; without it a page builds a String
- `rsx-tailwind`  a CSS build over the class names in your templates; needs node
- `rsx-htmx`  a click swaps what changed; the server renders from the shared layout down

**Absent:** Nothing. Every capability was chosen.

That is the framework's central rule: a capability nobody asked for is
not compiled and not linked. If you need one, add it to `Cargo.toml`
*and* name its plugin in `src/main.rs`. Nothing registers itself.

## Adding a route

A route is a file. `src/pages/about.rs` is `/about`;
`src/pages/users/[id].rs` is `/users/{id}`. **Write the file. That is
the whole of it** -- no `mod` line, no row to register, because there is
no list. `brocanth_pages::pages!` in `src/pages/mod.rs` reads this
directory while the crate compiles and writes both.

The verb comes off the handler's name: `handle` is GET, then
`handle_head`, `handle_post`, `handle_put`, `handle_patch`,
`handle_delete`, `handle_options`. A `pub fn handle_*` outside that
list is a build error naming the list, rather than a handler nothing
reaches; a page with no handler is a build error too. A private
`fn handle_*` is a helper and is left alone.

**Adding a file does not rebuild on its own** -- nothing referenced it
yet. Run `touch src/pages/mod.rs` after creating a page or a layout.
Editing or deleting one is noticed.

A handler returns a value and never writes a response itself. That is
what makes a half-written body on an error impossible rather than
unlikely.

## Views

The markup for a route is a `.rsx` file **next to the page that renders it**:
`src/pages/index.rsx` beside `src/pages/index.rs`. There is no second tree and
nothing to register -- `rsx::load_dir!("src/pages")` in `src/pages/mod.rs`
compiles them all into the binary. One file is one module, under `views`, so
`index.rsx` is `views::index` and `users/[id].rsx` is `views::users::_id_`.

### Layouts

`layout.rsx` wraps every page in its directory **and every directory below**,
and a page never names it: which layout wraps a page is a property of where
the page is. That is the Crystal page_router's rule for `layout.cr`.

They stack root to leaf, and **the chain is not written down anywhere**.
`html!` is a macro: it knows which file it was written in, walks up to
`src/`, and wraps the page in every `layout.rsx` it passes. So
`src/pages/users/layout.rsx` wraps the pages under `users/` inside the root
layout, and deleting that file removes exactly that layer with no other edit.

Every page uses the same import and the same call, whatever directory it is
in. Do not add a chain of your own; if a page is wrapped wrongly, the
directory tree is what to change.

A layout takes `children: Element`, and may also take `layout: &str`, which
`html!` fills with the URL prefix that layout covers. Those two are the only
parameters it fills, because it cannot know what a third one would mean.
A value every page shares comes from a `const` -- the root layout reads
`pages::TITLE` that way. A value belonging to one request belongs on the page
component, which the handler builds and which already has the context.

For a fragment that is not a document -- an htmx swap, a partial -- call
`render` instead of `html!`: the same thing with no shell.

**Adding a `layout.rsx` where there was none does not rebuild anything**,
because nothing referenced the file yet. Run `touch src/pages/mod.rs` after
creating one. Editing or deleting an existing layout is noticed.

A component is a function returning `Element`. Its parameters are its contract
with the handler, and a caller fills them as struct fields, so a field the
component does not declare is a compile error rather than a blank in the page.
A parameter of type `Element` receives children, which is all a layout is.

Reach a template from a handler with `html!`, and with nothing else:

```rust
pub fn handle(_ctx: &mut Ctx) -> Result<impl IntoResponse, Error> {
    html!(ctx, views::index::Index { title: TITLE })
}
```

It returns the handler's own `Result`, so there is no `Ok(..)` to write and a
template that bails propagates with `?`. For another status or a header,
compose with the other return shapes: `Ok((html!(ctx, tpl)?, 404))`.

Adding a page with markup is two files in one directory -- `<name>.rs` and
`<name>.rsx` -- and nothing else anywhere. Neither needs a line in
`src/pages/mod.rs`, because the directory is the registry.

Not every response is a page. A redirect is `Response::empty(303)` with a
header and no template anywhere near it.

An interpolated value is escaped on the way out. Templates are read at
**compile** time, so an edit needs a rebuild, and a template that does not
parse is a build failure on its own line rather than a 500.

## Static files

Two directories, and the difference matters. `assets/` is **fingerprinted**:
`site.css` is published at `/css/site.<hash>.css` and cached for a year.
`public/` is served **verbatim**, for names that cannot move -- `robots.txt`,
`favicon.ico`, anything linked to from outside.

Never write either URL by hand. `crate::assets::url("css/site.css")` takes the
logical path and returns the published one, and a name nothing publishes
panics there rather than 404ing in a browser.

A basename starting with `_` is an input and is never published, which is what
`assets/css/_tailwind.css` is.

Both directories are embedded in the binary. **Adding a file where there was
none does not rebuild anything**; run `touch src/assets.rs` after creating one.

## Partial navigation

Link to a route with the `Link` component, never a bare `<a>`:

```
<Link to={&crate::pages::routes::users::id::path(7)}>User 7</Link>
```

`to` takes what a route helper returns, so a link to a route that does not
exist is a compile error. It renders a real `<a href>` with `dp-boost` on it,
so the page still works with no JavaScript.

A layout marks what a swap may replace with `dp-layout={layout}`, on the
element wrapping **exactly** the children. Anything inside that element is
replaced with them, so a sidebar or a scroll position belongs outside it.

A request carrying `DP-Partial: n` drops the outermost `n` layouts, and
`html!` resolves that into a `match` over the chain. A handler never reads the
header and never changes for it.

## Tasks

A command is a `clap::Args` struct with `#[cmd]` on it, in its own file under
`src/commands/`, plus a `mod` line. It becomes a subcommand automatically —
registration happens at link time and there is no list to add it to.

```
brocanth --help      # lists this project's commands too
brocanth serve
brocanth css         # the CSS build; -W rebuilds on each change
```

The stylesheet is embedded, so a new one is a new binary. `css` rewrites
`src/assets.rs` to say so, which is what makes cargo notice.

## House style

- A comment says **why**, next to the decision, and what was chosen
  against. Not what the line does.
- A test name is a sentence describing the guarantee it protects.
- Prefer a type that cannot be built wrong over a check that can be
  forgotten.
- State a limit where someone would look for it rather than leaving it
  to be discovered.

## Framework reference

`docs/llm-authoring.md` in the brocanth checkout is the full brief: what
cannot compile and can therefore be relied on, what can still go wrong
and therefore needs a test, and the crate map.

## Reading a body

A handler never parses `ctx.body` itself. It declares a struct with
`#[derive(zod::Entry)]`, puts the rules on the fields, and calls
`ctx.body_as()` or `ctx.read()`. The rules are values: a `const`
shared by two structs is one rule, and `zod::accepts!` makes the
compiler check a literal against it.

Report every fault, never the first. `Faults` already holds them all
and `by_name()` groups them per field; a handler that returns after
the first one makes a person submit the form three times.

Do not write `?` on a `zod::Faults`. The blanket `From` on `Error`
turns any `std::error::Error` into a 500, and a bad body is a 422.
`body_as` is the call that gets the status right.

## Edge middleware

`src/app.rs` holds five commented registrations from
`brocanth-middleware`. Each encodes a fact about the deployment --
which proxy to trust, which host is canonical, which origins may call
-- so each is uncommented by somebody who knows that fact. Do not
enable them as a set, and do not invent an address or an origin to
make one compile.
